title: Check if One String Swap Can Make Strings Equal
statement:
The strings `s1` and `s2` have the same length. A swap chooses two positions of one string (they may be the same position) and exchanges the characters there.

Return `true` if you can make `s1` and `s2` identical by applying at most one swap, and that swap only to one of the two strings; return `false` otherwise. Strings that are already identical need no swap and give `true`.
constraints: s1 and s2 contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every swap and comparing works but costs O(n³). Look instead at the positions where `s1` and `s2` disagree. A single swap changes exactly two positions, so the strings can be fixed only if they disagree nowhere, or in exactly two places whose characters are crossed over.

## Approach

1. Walk both strings together and collect every index `i` where `s1[i] !== s2[i]` in `diff`.
2. As soon as `diff` holds a third index, return `false`: one swap can repair at most two.
3. If `diff` is empty, the strings already match: return `true`.
4. If it holds exactly one index, no swap helps: return `false`.
5. With two indices `first` and `second`, return whether `s1[first] === s2[second]` and `s1[second] === s2[first]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s1 = "bank"`, `s2 = "kanb"`. Index 0 differs (`b` vs `k`), indices 1 and 2 match, index 3 differs (`k` vs `b`), so `diff = [0, 3]`. Then `first = 0`, `second = 3`: `s1[0] = "b"` equals `s2[3] = "b"` and `s1[3] = "k"` equals `s2[0] = "k"`, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the strings.
- Space: O(1): `diff` never holds more than three indices.

## Pitfalls

- Exactly one mismatch can never be fixed, even though it is "close".
- Two mismatches are not enough on their own; the characters must be crossed (`"caa"` and `"aaz"` differ at two places but fail).
- Equal strings return `true`, because zero swaps is allowed.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `diff` | indices where the strings disagree |
| `i` | current position in both strings |
| `first`, `second` | the two mismatched indices when there are exactly two |

narration.2: Collect the indices where the two strings disagree.
narration.3: Walk both strings side by side.
narration.4: Do the characters at this position differ?
narration.6: A third mismatch is more than one swap can fix...
narration.12: No mismatches: the strings are already equal.
narration.15: Exactly one mismatch cannot be repaired by a swap.
narration.19: One swap works only if the two characters are crossed over.
